newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-ATP TOUR ANNOUNCE FIRST DOPING CASE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ATP TOUR ANNOUNCE FIRST DOPING CASE.

text.p: Spaniard Ignacio Truyol on Tuesday became the first tennis player to be suspended for doping, the ATP Tour announced.

"Mark Miles, chief executive officer ot the ATP Tour, announced today that Ignacio Truyol, 23, has violated the tennis antidoping rule for class I and II substances and has been suspended for one year, effective immediately," the ATP Tour said in a statement.
The ATP Tour did not say what substance Truyol, ranked 127 in the world, had taken or when he had undergone a dope test.
But it said a one-year penalty was applied in the case of class I products "which include steroids, masking agents and compounds".

"We are disappointed that there has been a violation of the tennis anti-doping rule, but professonal tennis cannot tolerate the use of banned substances that may compromise the integrity of the competition," Miles added.
